project.name: An Overnight Crew
project.goal: Keep a repository I own in good health, overnight, without me. Point this at MY REPO — set the GitHub workspace in Settings before starting. Every night, pick the single most valuable piece of maintenance available and do it properly rather than doing five things badly: a dependency that has moved and can be moved safely, a test that is flaky rather than failing, a warning the build has been ignoring, a broken link in the docs, a piece of dead code nothing reaches, a README instruction that is no longer true. Every change arrives as its own small pull request with a title that says what and a body that says why, and the full test suite must pass before it opens — a red PR waiting for me in the morning is worse than no PR. Never batch unrelated changes into one PR, and never open a second PR for something already open. If CI fails on the main branch, that outranks everything: diagnose it first and tell me what broke it. Do not refactor for taste, do not restructure anything I have not asked about, and if the most valuable thing tonight is nothing, say so and stop.
